items.title: Build the /roadmap build-status page
items.summary: A dependency-free page at /roadmap, backed by data/roadmap.json, that renders one table per status plus in-flight section tables. The living record of work on this project.
items.notes: Exists so work is tracked in one honest place before anything depends on it — storage is a single JSON file the assistant edits directly (no DB, no admin UI, no auth, by design). Kept dependency-free on purpose: no CDN, no build step, so it still opens in five years. Verified the /roadmap route returns 200 and /roadmap.json parses. Observed conflict I did NOT silently resolve: the pasted rules 3-4 (done newest-first, everything else oldest-first as a queue) contradict the follow-up 'order everything newest at the top' — I implemented rules 2-4 as written and flagged it for a ruling rather than quietly picking one. Ruling (2026-08-30): user chose to keep rules 2-4 as the default; header-click sort still overrides per-table (rule 5). Resolved with no code change.

items.title: Wellness Project exercise backfill
items.summary: Flask app finds empty Wellness Project (Health Connect) strength workouts and backfills them from the matching Speediance session's exercises, via an OAuth MCP client. Scheduled daily scan plus a manual button.
items.affects: wellness_client.py, reconcile.py, app.py (/wp/* routes), templates/wp_reconcile.html, tests/
items.notes: Design spec + 9-task TDD plan written and committed (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-30-wellness-project-backfill-design.md, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-30-wellness-project-backfill.md). Execution: subagent-driven development. Key design finding: Wellness Project exposes no REST API and no API key — its MCP endpoint IS the API, gated by OAuth (authorization_code + PKCE + refresh_token; no machine grant), so the app must connect once in a browser then refresh silently. The date+calories match key was exact across the live 90-day window. Built 2026-08-30 via 9-task subagent-driven development, all tasks reviewed clean and merged to main; automated suite 207 green (2 pre-existing unrelated e2e failures). The independent review gate caught and fixed two real bugs the plan itself had baked in: a CSRF state-expiry bypass (a stale OAuth `state` was still accepted) and a silent SSE data-loss (the MCP parser returned the first `data:` event, so a legal notification-before-result stream yielded an empty result). Two controller rulings: a dedup guard so one Speediance session can't fill two workouts, and a provenance note set directly rather than appending to the Health-Connect note. LIVE SMOKE TEST PASSED 2026-08-31: OAuth connect succeeded end-to-end (token stored 0o600); a real backfill filled Aug-29 'Miami Pull' (WP 696827) with its 5 exercises + provenance note and swept the other empty strength sessions, while the @ Gym and rowing/cardio entries were left untouched — the empty-only + dedup guards held. Observed surprise worth recording: Wellness Project's resolver RENAMES exercises to its own library (e.g. 'Barbell Bent Over Row' -> 'Row [Machine]', 'Seated Barbell Lat Pulldown' -> 'Close Grip Lat Pulldown'); loads and reps are exact, only the names/equipment tags remap. A 'keep literal name' flag is available if verbatim names are wanted later.

items.title: Move Wellness Project backfill into Settings
items.summary: Retire the standalone /wp/reconcile page and surface Connect + Backfill directly in the Settings page's Wellness Project card, with a spinner while a backfill runs.
items.affects: app.py (settings route passes wp_connected; wp_callback + /wp/reconcile redirect to /settings), templates/settings.html, templates/wp_reconcile.html (removed), tests/test_wp_routes.py
items.notes: User found the separate /wp/reconcile page a 'weird empty page' and asked for the controls to live in Settings, plus a spinner during the run. Connect/Backfill move into the existing Wellness Project card; /wp/reconcile and the OAuth callback now redirect to /settings so old links and the redirect_uri still resolve. Done + verified live 2026-08-31: /settings shows Connect when disconnected and a Backfill-now button with an animated spinner + live results panel when connected; /wp/reconcile returns 302→/settings; the OAuth callback lands on /settings; wp_reconcile.html deleted; suite 208 green (2 known-unrelated e2e failures). Results panel and all dynamic text use textContent (no innerHTML), honoring the project XSS rule.

items.title: Backfill: reclassify un-fillable sessions as skipped, not errors
items.summary: Sessions whose Speediance side has no usable data (deleted template, no logged sets) were reported as 'errors', alarming the user. Distinguish 'nothing to backfill here' (skipped) from a real write failure (error).
items.affects: app.py (_apply_match, _run_backfill report buckets), templates/settings.html (result panel), tests/test_wp_backfill.py
items.notes: Found while diagnosing the user's report: 'sync came up with errors instead of pushing today's workout.' Two independent causes. (1) Today's push didn't happen because the run fired before today's Speediance session / its Health-Connect import both existed; a re-run fills it — WP 756813 <-> Speediance 1107027, both 396 cal, exact same-day match. (2) Four old June/July empties genuinely cannot be filled (trainingId with a DELETED template, plus three sessions with no logged sets) and were mislabeled 'errors'. Fix: a per-session 'no usable Speediance data' outcome goes to a new 'skipped' bucket; only a failed WP write counts as an 'error'. The Settings results panel shows Applied / Skipped / Flagged / Errors so recurring un-fillable sessions read as informational, not failures. Done + verified live 2026-08-31: re-run produced applied 1 (today's WP 756813 <- Speediance 1107027, 7 exercises + provenance note), skipped 4 (the deleted-template + no-logged-sets sessions, now labeled SKIP with reasons), errors 0. 3 new tests (empty-detail -> skipped, deleted-template fetch -> skipped, WP-write-failure -> error); suite 211 green.

items.title: Install hourly backfill cron
items.summary: Run the backfill automatically every hour so a day's workout fills without anyone clicking.
items.notes: User asked to run it hourly. Installed in root's crontab at :15 every hour, hitting the loopback port (http://127.0.0.1:5001) directly — that path is behind nginx basic-auth on the public side but open on loopback, so NO password sits in the crontab. flock -n /tmp/wp-backfill.lock makes an overlapping run a no-op; each run appends an ISO timestamp + the JSON result to /var/log/wp-backfill.log. Verified live 2026-08-31: a run logged applied 0 / skipped 4 / errors 0 (today already filled; the 4 un-fillable oldies skipped as designed). The pre-existing 3am cleanup cron was left untouched. Note: the cron is machine state, not in the repo — docs/wp-backfill-cron.md documents the exact line to re-add on a rebuild.

items.title: Backfill uses the wrong detail route for Free Lift / Goal-Focused sessions
items.summary: The backfill fetches every non-course session from cttTrainingInfoDetail, which is always empty for Free Lift (type 1/7) and Goal-Focused (type 9) sessions. It should use freeTraining and aiCourseTrainingInfoDetail respectively.
items.affects: app.py (_apply_match), reconcile.py (Free Lift actionList/setList parsing), history detail route
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 while researching other Speediance projects for the MCP server. The three sessions the hourly backfill keeps 'skipping' as 'no loggable exercises' (2874609, 2644826, 2646057) are all Free Lift. Verified live: GET /api/app/trainingInfo/freeTraining/2874609 returns code 0 with actionList = Seated Barbell Row, 3 sets (setList[].summary + rawRepList). The route map comes from pookey/speediance-cli docs/api-notes.md (MIT): type 1/6/7 -> freeTraining, 2 -> courseTrainingInfoDetail, 3/5 -> cttTrainingInfoDetail, 4/9 -> aiCourseTrainingInfoDetail. Caveat before fixing: Free Lift per-set weights carry a 2.2 scale that pookey verified on kg accounts only; this account is lb, so the fix must reconcile against the session's own totalCapacity rather than blindly dividing. Verified live 2026-09-27: deployed, then a backfill run wrote Free Lift 2874609 onto WP 465896 (Seated Barbell Row 3×50 @ 20/25/30 lb). The History page now expands Free Lift, Quick and Goal-Focused sessions (live /api/history/detail checked for 2874609, 3056211, 264945). The other two old 'skipped' Free Lifts are outside the 90-day window; 2646057 also has no exercise picked, so it would be dropped anyway.

items.title: Investigate: does saving a template with presetId <= 0 shrink loads by 2.2?
items.summary: pookey/speediance-cli reports that a non-positive templatePresetId on POST /api/app/v2/customTrainingTemplate makes the server divide every weight and capacity by 2.2. This app sends -1 ('Custom') for movements without an RM preset.
items.notes: UNCONFIRMED for this app — logged so it is not lost. Earlier live checks showed 35 saved = 35 lb, so the app may not be affected (the field names may differ between clients, or the effect may be kg-account-only). Needs one controlled test: save a throwaway template with presetId -1 vs 1, read it back, compare weights. Do not change save logic until that test runs. Hypothesis (2026-09-27): the server treats these fields as POUNDS internally, so the ÷2.2 only bites kg-unit accounts; this account is lb, which would explain the earlier 35 -> 35 lb observation. Same logic applies to the template-level totalCapacity (the app sends the raw set-capacity sum). Still needs the one controlled test before being closed.

items.title: Standalone open-source Speediance MCP server (separate repo)
items.summary: A free, MIT-licensed, self-hostable MCP server replacing GM Manager (going paid): GM Manager's 19 tools plus additions, local stdio mode for Claude Desktop/Code and optional remote OAuth mode for claude.ai. Lives at /srv/speediance-mcp, its own git repo.
items.notes: Design in progress (brainstorming). Decisions so far: Python + official mcp SDK; two phases (core + local stdio first, remote OAuth second); single account per deployment; OAuth login verifies the deployment's own Speediance account; SQLite memory; MIT with hbui3's notice kept; synthetic test fixtures only. Research 2026-09-27: harvested endpoints from stozo04/speediance-cli and pookey/speediance-cli (both MIT); found userinfo/info (profile), freeTraining, aiCourse routes, getHeartRateGraph, and several write faults. Rowing done as a course or custom template has no per-interval data in any known route. Phase 1 BUILT 2026-09-27 on branch phase1 of /srv/speediance-mcp (21 commits, 198 offline tests, all 26 tools, CLI login/logout/status): 14 plan tasks each reviewed, plus a final whole-branch review whose 16 fixes landed (stale token after re-login, non-ASCII Windows timezone header, re-login race, preset-load rebuild guard, load-anchor merge, library download lock). NOT yet verified against the live Speediance account and not merged or published; remaining: merge decision, GitHub repo + push, live acceptance checklist (README), then phase 2 (remote OAuth). Live read-only check 2026-09-27 (reusing the web app's session, no login, no writes): all read tools worked on real data (templates, custom, Free Lift, course rowing with heart rate, Goal-Focused). It found two bugs, logged as #11 and #12, both fixed. Still not live-verified: write tools (create/update/delete/schedule), which need the user's go-ahead. Write tools live-verified 2026-09-27 (see the acceptance-test item). Phase 2 (claude.ai remote mode) live 2026-09-28 — see the phase 2 item. Remaining: publish the GitHub repo. CORRECTION 2026-09-29: the earlier note 'Rowing done as a course or custom template has no per-interval data in any known route' is now FALSE — GET /api/app/boatingSkiDataGraph/{uuid} returns per-point rowing telemetry for course rowing (verified live on session 2023440). See #42. PUBLISHED 2026-09-29: https://github.com/labatt/speediance-mcp (public, MIT keeping hbui3's notice). Published from a single fresh initial commit rather than the 56-commit history, because commit e275bac's phase-2 plan named a real host, public IP and DNS zone; rewriting history was blocked as destructive, so the clean-lineage branch `public-release` is what GitHub tracks (local `phase1` keeps the full history). The working tree was sanitised separately in 80893b8. Verified after each push: no host/IP in the published plan, and no credentials.json, *.db or .env in the tree. Update it by checking out public-release, `git checkout phase1 -- .`, commit, push. Also published: https://github.com/labatt/speediance-api — unofficial API notes (665 route names, verified endpoints with parameters and response fields, the session-slot model). Route and field names only; no Speediance code, credentials or personal data.

items.title: MCP bug: bilateral set loads read as half (one cable instead of both)
items.summary: speediance-mcp parsing.set_load took the larger side array for two-sided sets; a barbell set loads both cables, so Barbell RDL templated at 50/60/70 lb read back as 25/30/35. Halved session detail, strength profile, compare and suggest_load (would prescribe half the working weight).
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 in the read-only live check of MCP phase 1 (#10). Evidence: session 1168482 RDL set 1 leftWeights 25s + rightWeights 25s, weights 50s; template weights 50,60,70; userActionStatPage max 70/min 50. Fix: unpinned two-sided set = max(left)+max(right). The web app's history table uses detail.weights for bilateral sets and shows the correct total — not affected. FIXED on branch phase1 (a56be9e) and verified live 2026-09-27: RDL session 1168482 now reads 50/60/70, matching the template; suggest_load bases on 70 lb. Free Lift was checked too and is fine — its set `weight` is already the two-cable total (10 lb per side in rawRepList).

items.title: MCP bug: quick single-exercise sessions (type 7) parse with no exercises
items.summary: speediance-mcp: a type-7 session returned by freeTraining without actionList (e.g. a quick 'Standing Barbell Calf Raise' session) came back with 0 exercises; its sets are only in freeTrainingDetail.
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 in the MCP live check (#10): session 3056211 freeTraining dict has no actionList; freeTrainingDetail returns one list-shaped exercise. Fix: fall back to freeTrainingDetail when actionList is empty, shared by session detail and coaching. FIXED on branch phase1 (a3d6269) and verified live 2026-09-27: session 3056211 now parses Standing Barbell Calf Raise, 3 sets 40/45/50 lb, with no cardio/note; strength profile uses the same fallback.

items.title: Hourly WP backfill failing since 2026-08-31: window is 91 days, WP max is 90
items.summary: _wp_window() returns today-90 → today, which list_workouts counts as 91 days; Wellness Project rejects ranges over 90 days, so every scheduled backfill since 2026-08-31 ~15:15 has failed (~600 runs in /var/log/wp-backfill.log).
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 while verifying #8. The last successful run was 2026-08-31 14:15. Our window didn't change, so WP probably started enforcing the 90-day max then. Fix: an inclusive 90-day window (start = today - 89). Verified live 2026-09-27: the backfill connects again (10:39 run: no error).

items.title: Backfill tests overwrite the live wellness_reconcile_report.json
items.summary: tests/test_wp_backfill.py runs the real /wp/backfill route, which writes WP_REPORT_FILE in the app dir, so running the suite replaces the real last-run report (shown in Settings) with fake test data.
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27: after a test run the report showed the synthetic sp_training_id 2000001. Fix: tests patch WP_REPORT_FILE to a temp path. The next real run (hourly at :15) overwrites the bad report. Verified live 2026-09-27: a full test run left the real report file untouched (mtime unchanged); the next real run replaced the fake report.

items.title: WP backfill finds no targets: Wellness Project now prints 'kcal' instead of 'cal'
items.summary: reconcile._CAL_RE (\d+\s*cal) doesn't match WP's new '107 kcal' rows, so every workout's calorie parses as None and is_backfill_target rejects all of them. The backfill has had nothing to match against.
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 while verifying #8/#13: after fixing the window, the backfill connected but matched nothing. The list row for WP 465896 (2026-07-20, 8 min, empty Health Connect import) reads '· 8 min · 107 kcal'. Fix: accept 'cal' and 'kcal'. Verified live 2026-09-27: the dry run found 6 targets / 5 empty; a live run applied 4 (three custom sessions missed during the outage — 08-31, 09-06, 09-07 — plus the Free Lift) and correctly skipped 1 whose template was deleted.

items.title: Backfilled exercises get fuzzy-matched to the wrong WP exercise/equipment
items.summary: The backfill sends exercise NAMES to WP update_workout; WP resolves them fuzzily. 'Barbell Romanian Deadlift' became 'Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift [Dumbbell (per hand)]' (so its NSI/1RM read 50 lb as per hand) and 'Seated Barbell Row' became 'Seated Cable Row [Cable]'.
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 reading back WP 1013643 and 465896 after the #15 backfill. Needs research: whether WP add_exercises accepts an exercise id or equipment hint (list_exercises tool) so we can pin the right movement. Also check earlier backfills for the same mis-mapping. Not guessing a fix.

items.title: MCP login: remember the password by default, --no-remember to opt out
items.summary: speediance-mcp login currently asks 'Remember the password? [y/N]'. Make remembering the default (so expired sessions auto-relogin), drop the prompt, and keep --no-remember for token-only storage.
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-27. Trade-off explained to the user: with both the web app and the MCP server remembering the password, each re-login signs the other out (one session per account). Accepted; a shared-session option was offered and not chosen. Done 2026-09-27 on branch phase1 (c157a86): a plain login stores the password with no prompt (tested with input() patched to fail); --no-remember stores only the token; README and spec §15.14 updated; 204 tests pass. Not yet exercised with a real login, since that would sign out the web app's session.

items.title: Speediance session displacement: a new login kills the previous token (code 90 'offline'), whatever the device headers
items.summary: Live test 2026-09-27 (2 logins, user-approved): an Android-identity login killed the web app's token; an iPhone-identity login (different Mobiledevices) then killed the Android token. A displaced token answers code 90 'offline', not 91. Hypothesis that sessions are per device type: REFUTED for Mobiledevices. How GM Manager coexists with the phone is still unknown; a different App_type slot or a partner API are untested.
items.affects: research; web app api_client (code 90 handling); /srv/speediance-mcp client
items.notes: The web app auto-relogins only on 91, so after a phone login it shows 'offline'/signed out until the user clicks Log in, and that manual login is what signs the phone out. My test left the web app on a dead token; restored via /auth/relogin (verified: /api/history works again). Phone signed out as warned. UPDATE 2026-09-27 (user-approved probe): App_type values beyond SOFTWARE exist. WEB needs a request signature (1005 'Signature verification failed'; algorithm not public — not pursued). HARDWARE works with Versioncode '1' (omitting it gives 1003; 41000 gives 1004 'Invalid nonce string'). A byPass login with App_type HARDWARE did NOT kill the SOFTWARE session, and after the user logged into the Android app the HARDWARE session was still alive (code 0) while the web app's SOFTWARE token got 90 'offline'. A HARDWARE-issued token also works on requests sent as SOFTWARE/41000. => Log in as HARDWARE to get a slot that coexists with the phone (likely GM Manager's method). Open risks: HARDWARE may be the Gym Monster's own slot (a HARDWARE login might sign the machine out, unverified); writes and library content not yet tested with a HARDWARE-issued token.

items.title: MCP: treat code 90 'offline' (session taken by another login) as a session loss, not a generic rejection
items.summary: speediance-mcp only treats 91/401 as auth expiry, so when the phone signs in, every tool fails with 'Speediance rejected the request (code 90): offline' and the remembered-password re-login never fires.
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 in the displacement test. Policy question for the user: on 90, silently re-login (kicks the phone each time Claude is used after the phone) or report 'signed in elsewhere' and wait for an explicit login. Done 2026-09-27 as part of #20 (speediance-mcp fd8eaa2): code 90 now triggers the remembered-password re-login, which is safe now that logins use the HARDWARE slot. Unit-tested.

items.title: Log in as App_type HARDWARE so the web app and MCP server never sign out the phone
items.summary: Use the HARDWARE session slot (found in #18) for logins in the web app and speediance-mcp, keeping every other request as SOFTWARE/41000; treat code 90 as a session loss and silently re-login.
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-27. The user couldn't check whether the Gym Monster stayed signed in after the HARDWARE test login and said to assume it's OK — watch for the machine being signed out. Supersedes #19 (code 90 handling). Web app deployed 2026-09-27 (merged feat/hardware-session): after /auth/relogin with the HARDWARE login, verified live history list, session detail, exercise detail, and a throwaway template create → read back (Barbell Bent Over Row 5 @ 10) → delete. MCP on phase1 (fd8eaa2), tests pass. Still waiting for the user to confirm the Android app stayed signed in after the web app's HARDWARE re-login. VERIFIED 2026-09-27: the user confirmed the Android app was still signed in after the web app's HARDWARE re-login. Gym Monster status unverified (user not at the machine) — watch for it. REVERTED 2026-09-27: the user was signed out of the Gym Monster. HARDWARE is the machine's own slot (confirmed again with a single controlled HARDWARE login). Web app merge d307178 and MCP fd8eaa2 were reverted; superseded by the configurable client type (BIKE).

items.title: MCP live write-tool acceptance test
items.summary: Run create/get/update (rename + edit)/schedule/unschedule/delete on the real account with a throwaway template, including unilateral and Vita exercises, verifying read-back each step.
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-27. Uses a throwaway template named 'zz MCP test - delete me', with guaranteed cleanup. PASSED 2026-09-27 on the live account (second run, after a fix): create_workout verified (Barbell RDL 8@50/60 rest 90; Bent-Over Single-Arm Reverse Fly with sides 1,2; Vita High Pull level 5 / 30 s); get_workout matched; a rename-only update and an exercise edit (55/65) both verified; schedule on 2026-10-15 showed as a reservation next to the existing Goal-Focused workout; unschedule removed it; delete removed it (template count 9 before and after, no leftovers). Bug found and fixed (speediance-mcp 'fix: an in-place edit re-issues the template id'): the first run flagged every update as a duplicate because Speediance re-issues the numeric id on each save while keeping the code.

items.title: Configurable login client type (phone / gym-monster / nano / bike) for the MCP server and the web app
items.summary: Speediance keeps one session per client type. SOFTWARE = phone app, HARDWARE = Gym Monster, and NANO and BIKE are other machines' slots, which are free if you don't own them. Let users choose which slot our logins use; document it in the MCP README.
items.affects: /srv/speediance-mcp (config, client, cli, README); web app api_client.py + config.example.json
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-27 after live tests: a BIKE login (Versioncode 1) kept the Gym Monster signed in (user checked), left a SOFTWARE session alive, survived the phone's sign-in, and a BIKE login while the phone was signed in kept the phone signed in (user checked). HARDWARE confirmed twice to sign out the Gym Monster. NANO accepts Versioncode 1 like BIKE; a NANO login is not tested. Plan: MCP default 'bike'; this server uses web app=BIKE and MCP=nano so they don't share a slot. Implemented 2026-09-27. MCP phase1 c86b859: `--client-type` (default bike), stored in credentials; README section 'Choose a client type'; spec §15.15. Web app merged and pushed: config.json `login_client_type` (default phone; README table); this server is set to bike and signed in with it (history verified). Waiting for the user to confirm the phone stayed signed in. This server's MCP should log in with --client-type nano.

items.title: MCP phase 2: remote mode for claude.ai at https://mcp.example.com
items.summary: Streamable HTTP /mcp with OAuth (SDK endpoints + our provider), a sign-in page that only accepts this account, rate limiting, hashed tokens; deployed behind nginx/TLS under pm2.
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-28 ('I need to use it on claude.ai'). DNS created by the user's request: mcp.example.com A <your server IP> (Cloud DNS zone your-dns-zone). An SDK spike confirmed the full flow (register → authorize → our login → token → authed initialize). Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-28-phase2-remote-oauth.md (e275bac). DONE and verified live 2026-09-28: 4 plan tasks, each with a security fix round, then a final review and fix wave (store caps, `speediance-mcp revoke`, sticky logout, sign-in hardening); 305 tests. Deployed: pm2 app 'speediance-mcp' (serve --http on 127.0.0.1:8765), nginx site mcp.example.com (Let's Encrypt; per-IP limit_req on the OAuth endpoints), data dir /root/.config/speediance-mcp, signed in on client_type nano, unit lb. Bug found at deploy and fixed (51615a6): NANO/BIKE login responses have no 'unit', so the server stored kg; the known unit is now kept, and there's a --unit flag. The user connected claude.ai and it pulled their calendar; the server shows 1 client, 1 live token, 0 failures.

items.title: Avoided exercises: one shared list for the web app and the MCP server (select/deselect, with reasons)
items.summary: Mark/unmark exercises as avoided (optional reason) from the web app (Library toggle + filter, Settings list) and from claude.ai via MCP; generators never pick them; builder and MCP create/update warn. Single store: the MCP server's SQLite (exercise_marks), shared via a web app config path.
items.affects: web app: new avoided store + /api/avoided routes, library.html, settings.html, create.html, workout_gen.py, adaptive_training.py; speediance-mcp: memory.py (reason), tools
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-28 ('exercises I can't do ... select and deselect'). Design approved in chat. DONE and deployed 2026-09-28 (merged 242bdef, pushed to the fork). One shared store (the MCP DB's exercise_marks, with a reason column). Web: Library toggle (1041 toggles render) with an inline reason and an all/hide/only filter; Settings list with remove buttons and a persistent Library link; the builder warns without blocking; AI generate/refine never pick avoided moves (refine keeps ones already in your workout, with a truthful warning); adaptive_training.build_plan accepts avoided_ids (no caller yet); store errors never break pages (503 on writes); tests isolated from the live DB. MCP: mark_exercise reason, reasons shown in reads, create/update flag avoided moves. Live check: /api/avoided lists the 21 avoided marks set via claude.ai; /library, /settings and /create all 200. Two review rounds on the web side, one on the MCP side.

items.title: MCP bug: get_calendar drops phone-health activities (walks, AeroRow rows) that GM Manager showed as otherActivities
items.summary: speediance-mcp's get_calendar skips history rows imported from the phone health app (belongUserHealth), so off-machine work such as walks and AeroRow rowing is invisible and weekly load is understated. GM Manager returned these per day as otherActivities.
items.notes: Reported 2026-09-28 by the user relaying claude.ai's comparison with GM Manager: no otherActivities on any day in September. The exclusion was deliberate (to keep gym-session counts right) but dropped the data entirely. items.title: Progress page part 2: muscle balance (per-muscle volume, push:pull, upper:lower, not trained in 30 days) + MCP get_muscle_balance
items.summary: Per-muscle volume from each session's exercises, with the main muscle weighted 100% and assisting muscles 50% (stated on the page); push:pull and upper:lower ratio bars; muscles not trained in N days. The same numbers are exposed to claude.ai as a new MCP tool, get_muscle_balance(days).
items.affects: web app progress page + speediance-mcp new tool
items.notes: From the GM Manager Progress evaluation (#36). User queued all three parts 2026-09-28, including the figure. DONE 2026-09-29. MCP (source of truth, fac565d): speediance/muscles.py + get_muscle_balance(days) — tool 29. Web (independent twin, no MCP dependency): muscle_balance.py, GET /api/progress/muscles?days=N, and the /progress page. Key finding: the cached exercise library ALREADY carries mainMuscleGroupList/auxiliaryMuscleGroupList for all 1,040 movements, so per-muscle analysis costs no extra API calls; session payloads only carry the coarse trainingPartId2. 17 muscles over 8 body parts. Decisions: main 100% / assisting 50% (stated on the page, since the attributed total then exceeds the weight lifted); Full Body joins neither chain (counting it both ways flatters every ratio); a muscle that only ever assists is never listed as 'not trained' (that would be a catalog artefact); timed/level work carries no volume and is surfaced as unweightedExercises rather than counted as zero. Verified: both implementations agree exactly on the same 10-day window (push:pull 0.91, upper:lower 2.62, not trained Adductors + Side Delts). 30-day live read: push:pull 0.48, upper:lower 3.51 — pull and upper body dominate.

items.title: Extract the Speediance phone app's API endpoint list (static strings only)
items.summary: Pull every /api/ path from the Android app's compiled Flutter library (libapp.so) to find undocumented routes (Wellness+, profile/settings updates, etc.). Static only: nothing is run and the account isn't touched.
items.affects: research (scratchpad); findings may feed the MCP/web roadmap
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-29 ('just to find the end points'). Don't publish Speediance code or secrets; endpoint names only. DONE 2026-09-29: static extraction from libapp.so in split_config.arm64_v8a.apk (base.apk holds only Java class names; Flutter code lives in the ABI split). 665 real routes in 174 resource groups after dropping the app's own source-file paths; list at docs/research/speediance-app-endpoints.md. Route names only: request/response shapes are unknown until probed. Headline finds: mobile/userHealth/* (recovery, sleep, trainingLoad, healthScore, physicalCondition), app/userDataStat/trainingPartFatigueInfo (muscle fatigue), app/userBody/* and mobile/bodyFatMeasurement/* (body weight/composition), app/userinfo/save|setting and app/userPreference (profile/settings writes), app/strengthScore/summary. LIVE READS 2026-09-29 (user: 'then run those reads'; GET only, nano token, relogin disabled, 2.5 s spacing): ROWING — GET /api/app/boatingSkiDataGraph/{uuid} (the session's uuid, NOT trainingId; courseTrainingInfo/{id} carries uuid and existBoatingSkiDataGraph) returns pointDataList: one point per ~3 s with time, spm, resistance, power (W), pace (s/500m), and the course's target band minSpm/maxSpm/minResistance/maxResistance — the per-interval rowing data no known route had (177 points for a 530 s HIIT row). Also working: mobile/userHealth/trainingLoad/dateRange?startDate&endDate (daily TRIMP + recommended band), app/userDataStat/trainingPartFatigueInfo (per-muscle fatigue 1-3 + muscleLoadStatus), app/strengthScore/summary (empty for this account), mobile/userHealth/newIndex/healthScore (walking, nutrition, bodyAge, wellnessMonitor), app/userBody/current (weight/height/BMI/body fat), app/userPreference (device toggles). Parameter error (params unknown, not guessed further): userDataStat/boatingSki*, userHealth/recovery|sleep|physicalCondition|calendar/scores|healthDataIndicators, userBody/stat. app/userinfo/setting is POST-only (a write, not tried). mobile/muscleLoad/detail gives server error 500.

items.title: Per-interval rowing view (session detail page + MCP session tool)
items.summary: For rowing sessions that have boatingSkiDataGraph data, show stroke rate, power, pace/500m and resistance over time against the course's target SPM/resistance band, with per-interval splits (work vs rest) and target hit-rate. Expose the same through the MCP's session tool so Claude can coach rowing intervals.
items.affects: api_client.py, session_detail.py, session detail template (web); /srv/speediance-mcp speediance/api.py + tools/sessions.py
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-29 ('yes'). Found via the app endpoint extraction (#41). Route: GET /api/app/boatingSkiDataGraph/{uuid} — keyed on the session uuid (courseTrainingInfo/{id} has it), NOT trainingId; only call when existBoatingSkiDataGraph is true. Points every ~3 s: time, spm, resistance, power (W), pace (s/500m), minSpm/maxSpm/minResistance/maxResistance. Intervals should be derived from changes in the target band. Open questions for design: pace in the first seconds is a startup artifact (587 s/500m at t=0); spm reads 0 on some points — verify whether that means rest or a dropped sample. Tests use synthetic fixtures only. EXISTING CODE REVIEW 2026-09-29. Web app: cardio_stats.py derives summary-only metrics (pace500/speedMs/calPerMin/energyKJ/avgWatts/completion/rpe) from session totals, with a JS twin in static/workout-logic.js::deriveCardioStats that must stay in sync (shared oracle: trainingId 2023440 — the same HIIT row used for the boatingSkiDataGraph probe); /api/cardio/trend caches per trainingId in cardio_trend_cache.json; templates/history.html renders tiles + a metric-switching trend chart (fmtPace, CARDIO_METRICS). Detection is CARDIO_COURSE_TYPES={2} with a standing TODO to widen — replace with existBoatingSkiDataGraph, a precise flag. MCP server: speediance/parsing.py::is_cardio ALREADY tests existBoatingSkiDataGraph; derive_cardio_stats mirrors the web app; intervals_from()+set entries already map distance/pace/spm->strokeRate, but ONLY for guided cardio (type 7, freeTrainingDetail). ACTION: tools/sessions.py ROWING_GAP_NOTE tells Claude 'Per-interval rowing data isn't available for rowing done as a course or custom workout' — now false and user-visible on claude.ai; replace it with a boatingSkiDataGraph fetch keyed on find_uuid(), reusing intervals_from's row shape so both cardio paths return one schema. DONE 2026-09-29. MCP (source of truth, commit 228f718, 411 tests): speediance/api.py rowing_graph(uuid); parsing.session_uuid() — needed because find_uuid() gates on showHeartGraph, which a rowing session sets to 0; parsing.rowing_telemetry() cuts blocks where the target band changes; tools/sessions.py returns `rowing` and the note now only appears when a session genuinely has neither intervals nor telemetry. Web app (independent twin, no MCP dependency per the user's 'the mcp should be able to be standalone without the web app'): rowing_stats.py, api_client.get_rowing_graph(), GET /api/session/<id>/rowing (uuid resolved server-side from the account's own session summary, never from the query string), and a per-block table in the history detail panel. 12 new tests; suite 343 pass / 2 pre-existing e2e failures. Both open questions resolved from the real data: spm==0 marks non-stroking samples (flywheel spin-up, pauses, cool-down) and is counted as rest and excluded from every average — that also removes the startup pace artifact, so no time-based fudge was needed. Finding worth keeping: session totals badly understate rowing effort. Verified session 2023440 reads 56 W at 4:57/500m overall but 265 W at 4:02/500m while actually stroking, because 93 s of its 531 s was rest.

items.title: Crack request params for recovery / sleep / readiness / daily-condition routes
items.summary: Check whether the account has real recovery/sleep data (mockReport/hasReal*), then decompile libapp.so with Blutter to read the exact request parameters, then confirm with one read per route.
items.affects: research (scratchpad); feeds Health & Wellness decisions and MCP/web features
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-29 ('yes' to: two data-existence reads, then Blutter). Static decompile runs locally; live calls are GET only, nano token, no relogin, spaced. Endpoint names only; no Speediance code published. 2026-09-29: hasRealRecoveryData=false, hasRealSleepData=true (recovery screen likely shows sample data; sleep is worth cracking). App is Flutter 3.44.7 / Dart 3.12.2. Build deps installed (cmake, ninja-build, pkg-config, libicu-dev, libcapstone-dev); Blutter cloned (4a60ac6, 2026-08-18) to the scratchpad. Running it was blocked by the session's permission guard (it executes freshly downloaded code) — waiting on the user. DONE 2026-09-29. Blutter's output is structure-only (class/method skeletons, no instruction bodies), so params weren't recoverable statically; instead the candidate key names were harvested from the app's string pool and only existing ones were tried. ANSWER: the date parameter is `dateStr` (YYYY-MM-DD). Confirmed working: mobile/userHealth/recovery/detailByDate?dateStr (returns recoveryScoreResp/nightHrvResp/nightRestingHeartRateResp/sleepResp/muscleLoadResp, all empty for this account — no overnight HRV source), mobile/userHealth/sleep?dateStr ({sleep, targetSleepMin}), and mobile/userHealth/physicalCondition/detailByDate?dateStr — which returns REAL readiness data: physicalConditionValue, physicalConditionScore, fitness, fatigue, trainingStatus, plus physicalConditionParam.trainingStatusScore/trainingStatusScoreAvg. On 2026-09-28: score 90.4, fitness 5.99, fatigue 6.81, trainingStatus 1.14, trainingStatusScore 93.6 (avg 87.36). mobile/userHealth/sleep/rhythm is POST (code 12), not GET. Still unknown after bounded probing: calendar/scores, newIndex/healthDataIndicators, physicalCondition/listDailyDateRange — none accept dateStr, startDate/endDate, startDateStr/endDateStr, beginDateStr, monthStr or dateType. Implication for the Health & Wellness decision: recovery/readiness cards would be EMPTY (no wearable), but training status (fitness vs fatigue) is real and daily.

items.title: Body map redrawn: anatomical silhouette, front/back labels, hover tooltip
items.summary: Replace the blocky figure with a bezier silhouette, label the views, remove the crotch-shaped adductor block, and add a hover tooltip giving muscle, volume and status.
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-29: 'looks like a two year old drawed it', front vs back indistinguishable, 'the left one looks like it has a genital in between the legs', and hover should name the muscle and its status. Fixed: bezier silhouette with regions following the body; FRONT/BACK headings; adductors moved to inner-thigh slivers on each leg; abs narrowed with segment detail; HTML tooltip with muscle, volume and a plain-word status (not trained / light / moderate / worked hard / most worked); hovering lights up BOTH sides, since left and right are one muscle. Colour ramp took three goes, recorded in code comments so they aren't repeated: blue->amber interpolates through grey (hardest-worked muscles rendered mud); adding teal+yellow fixed the mud but made a rainbow with no readable order; final is magma-style (indigo->purple->red->orange->pale yellow), monotone in brightness. Verified by rendering the page headless and looking at it, not by trusting the markup. 2026-09-29 follow-up (user: 'brighten up the colors', 'the gray words against the black background are unreadable'): the silhouette fill went #1b2330 -> #3f4a63 with lighter outlines, untrained #273244 -> #5a6478, and the whole magma ramp was lifted, so the head, hands and torso no longer read as holes. Separately and app-wide, Tailwind's dim greys are tuned for white backgrounds: on #0d1117, text-gray-600 measured 2.50:1 and text-gray-500 3.91:1, both below the 4.5:1 WCAG AA floor. layout.html now overrides the three dim steps to 6.28:1 / 7.55:1 / 10.33:1 centrally rather than editing ~280 class uses across the templates. 2026-09-29 second follow-up — the FIRST contrast fix never applied at all. The Tailwind play CDN injects its stylesheet at runtime AFTER the template's own <style>, so a bare `.text-gray-600` override loses the cascade at equal specificity and is silently ignored; reading the computed colour in a headless browser showed the page still serving Tailwind's rgb(75,85,99) despite the commit claiming measured ratios. Lesson: for any Tailwind-play-CDN override in this app, prefix the selector with `body` (or otherwise raise specificity) and VERIFY with getComputedStyle — inspecting the markup proves nothing, because the markup was correct both times. Also raised the caption floor: 10-11px text (47 uses across 9 templates) is hard to read even at a passing contrast ratio, so `body [class~="text-[10px]"]` and the 11px equivalent are forced to 12px. Final: rgb(166,176,195) at 12px, confirmed by getComputedStyle. 2026-09-29 third follow-up (user: 'where are the triceps in the body picture'): they were drawn but unfindable — a 10x26 crescent (area 270) on the INNER edge of the upper arm, while being the third most worked muscle. Redrawn to span the upper arm (area 445); biceps share the shape on the front and the forearms were widened to match. Region sizes are now checked with getBBox in a headless browser rather than judged by eye — scratchpad/probe2.js prints every region's bounding box and area per view. 2026-09-29 fourth follow-up (user: 'add the side delts .. and when you put your mouse over a muscle group in the volume by muscle table, highlight the muscle on the body image'): Side Delts added as a lateral cap on BOTH views (front/rear delts moved inboard) — previously the shoulder cap did duty as front or rear delts alone, so a muscle listed as 'not trained' had no region to look at. Highlighting refactored into one setHighlight(muscle, on) keyed on the name and applied across both figures AND the table row, so the link works in both directions: table row -> body, and body -> row. Verified by driving hovers in a headless browser and reading back stroke colour and row class (scratchpad/probe3.js), not by inspecting the handlers.

items.title: E2E workout tests polluted the live account and are now opt-in
items.summary: test_e2e_workouts.py creates real workouts on the live Speediance account and failed before cleanup, leaving 30 E2E_TEST_* templates behind. Delete them and stop a plain test run from writing to the account.
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-29 ('delete all the E2E_TEST workouts'). Deleted 30 templates matching the strict pattern E2E_TEST_(CUSTOM|PRESET)_<digits>; the 9 real workouts were listed first and left untouched. Root cause: the tests ran on every plain `pytest` invocation, created a workout each, and failed before their cleanup — they were also the long-standing '2 pre-existing failures'. They now require SPEEDIANCE_E2E=1, so the suite is 415 passed / 2 skipped and never writes to the live account by accident.

items.title: Evaluate GM Manager's features for inclusion (series): 4. Cardio
items.summary: GM Manager's Cardio page: VO2max / Fitness (CRF) / Resting HR / Blood O2 cards, daily trend charts for heart rate, blood oxygen and steps, a click-through modal with Total/Average/Peak plus a per-day table, and a .fit upload (Garmin/Wahoo/Coros) with a cycling FTP for power-based TSS.
items.notes: Screens supplied 2026-09-29. EVALUATION. What their own account shows: VO2max, Fitness (CRF) and Resting HR are ALL EMPTY — matching the #43 finding that those need overnight HRV/resting HR from a paired device. Blood O2 (91%), heart rate (74-94 bpm daily) and steps (up to 10,077) DO have data. So the four-card row is 3/4 dead weight for this account. FLAW NOT TO COPY: their modal shows a 'Total' for heart rate (587.5bpm) and blood oxygen (594%) — summing a rate and a percentage across days is meaningless. Average and Peak are sound; Total should exist only for steps (and distance/calories). WORTH COPYING: the per-metric modal with a per-day table behind each chart, and their honest note 'today so far — still being counted, and included in Total and Average, the same way the Speediance app counts it'. SOURCING (probed read-only 2026-09-29): app/userDataStat/heartRateStatIndex WORKS with no params and returns watchType, max/min HR and time in 5 HR zones (timeLevel1-5 + timeLevelList) — that is a better card than a bare resting HR. mobile/userHealth/newIndex/healthScore gives today's step count (walking.value). app/watchMsg/getHeartRateGraph already gives per-session HR (MCP get_heart_rate). Still unsourced: a DAILY series for HR, SpO2 or steps — heartRateStatByDateType returns 500 on every param shape tried, and newIndex/healthData and appIndex/healthData both 500 bare. RECOMMENDATION: don't build the four-card row as-is. Build HR zones + steps + per-session HR first (all sourceable today), and treat the daily HR/SpO2 series as blocked on cracking heartRateStatByDateType. Skip the .fit upload for now: it needs a .fit parser, and their own copy says it isn't fed into training load.

items.title: Evaluate GM Manager's features for inclusion (series): 5. History
items.summary: GM Manager's History: date range, four summary cards (Sessions, Volume, Calories, Time), a session table, and a detail modal with muscle chips and a per-set breakdown.
items.notes: Screens supplied 2026-09-29. EVALUATION: our /history already matches their list one-for-one (same four summary cards, same columns) and the detail modal is richer — we add a felt-rating panel, a muscle-group rollup with per-group completion, a Coach's read, per-exercise power/resistance/ROM charts with force/ROM/balance scores, star ratings and a JSON export, none of which they have. ONE REAL GAP: they print every set as compact text — '1 27 lb x 10/10', '2 30 lb x 8/8' — and for unilateral work 'L 20 lb x 12/12 . R 20 lb x 12/12' with '3 sets per side . 1,680 lb vol'. We show the chart and the summary but never the plain per-set numbers, which are the thing you actually read back when repeating a session. Proposed as #49. BUG FOUND AND FIXED while comparing: phone-health imports carry no `type`, so our table rendered the literal 'Type undefined' (Sep 1 and Sep 2 rows). Now labelled 'Phone health'. CORRECTION 2026-09-29: the 'one real gap' claimed here did not exist — we already print every set with L/R labels. See #49 for what was actually different (per-side counting and numbering). The gap was an artefact of reviewing a scrolled screenshot instead of the rendered DOM.

items.title: History detail: unilateral sets counted per side, with paired numbering
items.summary: Under each exercise in the session detail, list every set as compact text — weight x completed/target reps, per side for unilateral work, with 'sets per side' and the exercise's volume.
items.notes: From the #48 History evaluation: the one thing GM Manager's detail does that ours doesn't. Our per-set data is already fetched (setLog drives the charts), so this is presentation only. Respect the two-cable rule: a unilateral set shows each side separately, a bilateral barbell set shows the TOTAL, never one cable's number. CORRECTION 2026-09-29: the premise of this item was WRONG. Our detail modal already listed every set (#, reps completed/target, weight, volume) INCLUDING L/R side labels — the earlier evaluation was made from a screenshot scrolled past that table, and I should have checked the rendered DOM before claiming a gap. What was genuinely different: a unilateral exercise logs each side as its own set, so the header read '6 sets' for what was really 3 per side, and numbering ran L1 R2 L3 R4 L5 R6, which reads as six unrelated sets. Now 'N sets per side' (only when both sides were worked evenly) with paired L1 R1 L2 R2 L3 R3 numbering.
